summary: C-0004: The emerging 2022-2025 synthesis dissolves the state/non-state dichotomy: predictive coding/active inference provides a unified framework where 'state-like' precision-weighting and 'non-state-like' priors/expectancy are two sides of one mechanism
content: CLAIM C-0004: The most recent theoretical work (2022-2025) converges on predictive-processing/active-inference as a unifying framework that dissolves the classical state-vs-non-state dichotomy. Lynn et al. 2022 extend Kirsch's response expectancy INTO predictive coding. Jamieson et al. 2025 show dissociated-control, absorption, and response-expectancy can all be modelled in one active-inference framework. Terhune 2024 frames the objective/subjective reality balance as prediction-gain vs prediction-error-gain. SATH (Zahedi et al. 2024) explains both objective and subjective phenomena. Cold control (Dienes & Perner) provides a metacognitive mechanism. Ability-based models (Lush/Dell) go further and reject BOTH state and nonstate. SUPPORTS: synthesis position; the dichotomy is widely considered a false one in current literature. LIMIT: these are largely theoretical/computational proposals with testable but not-yet-decisively-tested predictions; predictive coding itself is debated in neuroscience.
